messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: alert: Elevated 502/504 rates on /v1/generate (edge region us-east-1). 5-min spike -> 18% error rate, latency tail > 4s. Paging oncall.
oncall-alex: ack. looking now — dropping into traces. can someone confirm customer impact? any dashboards showing spike by customer?
support-tom: several customers in EU reporting timeouts in chat sessions. ticketing shows retries from mobile clients. putting a note in status page draft.
sre-jen: I'm seeing gateway 502s originating from proxy-layer 3. Error rate correlates with requests that have long KV cache misses. traces are sparse — most spans missing span_id on the proxy hop.
eng-maria: hmm, we don't have full proxy-side tracing enabled in prod sampling right now. likely sampling config change rolled last week. quick mitigation: route traffic to fallback pool with slightly lower max-concurrency. can we change routing policy for 5 min?
oncall-alex: yes, do that. set route to fallback-compat, 20% fallback, then increase if needed. also enable debug logging on proxy instances in the affected ASG.
eng-maria: rolling policy update in progress: runbook cmd:
```
redwoodctl routing update --policy edge --fallback-pct 20 --region us-east-1
``` 
eng-maria: enabling proxy debug via ssm: `aws ssm send-command --document-name DebugModeOn ...` — switching loglevel to debug for 2h. adding temporary sampling tweak: increase proxy trace sampling to 100% for 10m for the affected ASG.
obs-bot: note: trace-sampling bumped to 100% on proxy-asg-us-east-1 by eng-maria. logs routed to ephemeral log-proxy stream.
sre-jen: starting a lightweight log-proxy (tcp forward) to central collector since our fluentd pipeline is dropping some proxy logs. command:
```
kubectl -n infra run tmp-log-proxy --image=logproxy:latest --env=DEST=s3://incident-logs/tmp
```
support-tom: created incident channel for affected customers and posted an initial status: "Mitigations underway, toggled fallback routing, collecting more traces" :eyes:
product-ana: are customers hitting specific models? need to assess potential model-level timeouts.
eng-maria: looks like large-context requests (seq_len>4096) have more failures. increasing model-worker timeout temporarily to 12s for compatibility tier.
oncall-alex: summary for handoff: 1) fallback routing set to 20% (eng-maria) 2) proxy loglevel debug enabled (eng-maria) 3) trace sampling 100% for ASG (eng-maria) 4) temporary log-proxy forwarding logs to incident bucket (sre-jen) 5) model-worker timeout increased to 12s for compat tier (eng-maria) 6) support notified customers (support-tom).
oncall-alex: leaving pager in 15m; handing to secondary oncall (sre-jen) — please continue trace capture and confirm if error rate drops below 2% and tail latency <1.5s.
sre-jen: taking over. next steps: capture a 30s trace dump, look for missing span ids -> if still missing, run quick shim to add request-id header at ingress to preserve trace context.
eng-maria: quick shim (example) — add header injection in envoy config:
```
- name: x-trace-proxy
  value: "%REQ(x-request-id)%"
```
sre-jen: deployed shim to canary proxy pool. starting trace aggregation now.
obs-bot: metric update: error rate fell from 18% -> 6% after fallback routing and timeout bump. latency p95 down 30%.
support-tom: updating customers: "We implemented routing fallback and are collecting more traces. Expect intermittent errors to subside within next 30m." :white_check_mark:
oncall-alex: final note for postmortem: missing proxy-side spans + recent sampling change were primary gaps. recommend adding an automated check that verifies proxy trace headers preserved on deploy and a playbook to spin up log-proxy within 2 minutes.
product-ana: logging follow-up: track which customers experienced degraded quality and offer credits if SLA breached. I'll sync with bizops.
sre-jen: leaving final handoff — all mitigations still active, monitoring. will escalate if error rate >5% or traces still incomplete. closing active pager for me but keeping thread pinned for post-incident notes.
incident-bot: incident resolved: error rate back to baseline (<1.5%) after 28m. actions taken stored at /incidents/3635009999/runbook.log :tada:"
